_comment: What to read out of Mistral's two public price sources.
MODELS come from `source`, https://docs.mistral.ai/models. Its index lists the
models currently offered as cards, and each card's page carries a machine-readable
price object with the unit stated per figure. PRODUCTS come from
`products_source`, https://mistral.ai/pricing/api, which is the only place web
search, code execution, image generation, libraries, data capture and the two
classifier models are priced at all.
Neither source alone is complete, which is why both are read. An earlier version
read only the pricing page and silently missed four priced models: OCR 4.0, OCR 3,
Leanstral 1.5, and Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2 -- the last of which the pricing page
had dropped while Mistral was still selling it, so this repository published it as
withdrawn. A marketing page is not an inventory.
Neither half names a model. Which models exist is read from the docs index every
week; a model Mistral adds is published on the next run, one it retires keeps its
last observed prices under an 'absent_since' stamp. There is no hand-written model
list and there must not be one.
KEYS ARE THE NAMES EACH SOURCE STATES, lowercased: 'ocr 4.0', 'mistral medium 3.5',
'web search'. Not API model ids. Those are published beside them in 'api_ids',
read from the 'names' array the same docs pages stream, most specific first and
in the order given.
BOTH THE INVENTORY AND THE IDS COME FROM MISTRAL'S OWN PAGES, and from nothing
else. No other provider's data feeds this block, and it must never be made to: an
aggregator can confirm that a string is a real Mistral id, but not that Mistral
still sells it. Resellers lag retirements, and can hold contracts that keep a model
callable through them for months after it leaves Mistral's public API.
_comment_denominators: The docs pages state a unit per figure, as a 'denominator' string, split into
'input' and 'output' lists. The table below is the whole translation: an input
figure denominated '/M Tokens' is in_per_mtok, the same string on the output side
is out_per_mtok. A denominator missing from the table is NOT guessed at -- the unit
is part of the field name and there is no honest field to put an unrecognised
figure in -- so that one figure is skipped, the run reports it, and every other
'labels' overrides the denominator when a row names itself: GLM 5.2 states two
input figures denominated '/M Tokens', ordinary and 'Cached input', which would
A figure of 0 is skipped rather than published. On this source that is not the
ambiguous zero a broken parser produces: the pages state 'free' separately, so a
zero means 'this side is not billed' -- Voxtral TTS charges for the audio it
generates and nothing for the text it is given.
_comment_rows: 'rows' is the same idea for the pricing page's products, which state their unit in
a row label instead. A label is matched exactly first; failing that, the longest
entry below that the label STARTS with wins. The prefix rule exists for two rows
only -- training cost and storage cost -- where Mistral appends an explanatory
sentence to the label, one of which quotes a fee that will itself change.
'products' lists the cards to read off that page. Everything else on it is a model,
and models come from the docs site. A name here that matches no card is not an
error: the card is simply gone, and the entry is dated and kept like any other.
_comment_currency: priceUsd is read and USD is published. Both sources also state EUR, and the two
are genuinely different prices rather than a conversion of one another -- 1.25 EUR
against 1.50 USD. No conversion is performed anywhere in this repository.
